common_name: Sweet almond verbena / sweet almond bush
look_here_first: Find a mature opposite leaf and an intact axillary flowering raceme. Measure 5–10 fully expanded leaves (often 4–9 × 1.5–6 cm) and inspect the long, loose, often flexuose raceme: individual flower bases are visibly separated. Compare against A. gratissima's generally smaller leaves and short, crowded racemes. Do not rely on fragrance or white flower color.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew POWO accepts Aloysia virgata and gives native range Peru through Brazil and northern Argentina, not Texas; cultivated/encounter taxon in approved source pool, not a confirmed Texas target-zone native.

morphology_keys.habit: Woody aromatic shrub, sometimes large; often branching with long flowering shoots.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, simple, ovate to elliptic, often acute and toothed; commonly 4–9 cm long × 1.5–6 cm wide; leaf hairiness and tooth depth variable.
morphology_keys.racemes: Lax, frequently flexuose/zigzag, axillary racemes; flower bases remain individually visible, sometimes several racemes per leaf axil.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small tubular white flowers; use the raceme's structure rather than color or scent.
best_field_traits: Opposite mature leaves often substantially larger than A. gratissima
Flowering axes lax and flexuose, with separated flower bases
Usually toothed leaf margins, but variable; measure several mature leaves

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. gratissima typically has much smaller leaves and shorter, dense flower racemes; Lantana urticoides has flowers packed into rounded heads rather than extended racemes; Verbena halei is herbaceous with spikes, not a woody shrub.
comparisons.cautions: Leaf size, teeth, and hairiness overlap within Aloysia; never use a single leaf or aroma as proof. Confirm inflorescence architecture, multiple mature leaves and woody habit.

diagnostic_image_needs: Whole shrub with intact flowering branches
Side-on loose/flexuose raceme showing individually separated flower bases
Mature leaf with scale and opposite attachment
Paired side-by-side comparison with Aloysia gratissima dense raceme
